title: Patch Harbor brief and Rollout Garden schedule (Dec 2026) - draft
body:
OVERVIEW:

This doc is a compact briefing for the Dec 2026 Patch Harbor rollout (internal name: Rollout Garden). Intended audience: release engineers, on-call SREs, product PM for Hosted API, and the dedicated-capacity ops lead. Draft status — working notes, not final.

High-level objective:
- Ship a small-surface patch (safety fixes and batching tunings) to hosted API with minimal user-facing disruption, verify telemetry for performance regressions, and validate new backoff logic.
- Keep the change surface limited (API contract unchanged), route 1% traffic for first 60m (canary), escalate to 25% after green, then 100% with gradual ramp and surge caps.

SCOPE (what's in / out):
- In: serving-runtime batching tweak, KV cache TTL adjustment, small prefork change to keep GPU warm, and fallback routing policy update for low-capacity region B.
- Out: model weight changes, quantization changes, major config flips, or client SDK changes.

TIMELINE & ROLLOUT GARDEN SCHEDULE (local times UTC):
- T-72h (Dec 05 09:00 UTC): Final signoff on canary gating checklist. Confirm capacity reservations and smoke tests.
- T-24h (Dec 07 09:00 UTC): Dry-run on staging with production traffic replay; telemetry baselines captured.
- T-6h (Dec 07 21:00 UTC): Release binary built, sha512 published, security scan green.
- T-1h (Dec 07 02:00 UTC): Preflight meeting (15m), roll-out captain assigned, canary SREs on standby.
- T+0 (Dec 08 03:00 UTC): Deploy to canary pool (1% global). Start 60m observation window.
- T+60m: If green, expand to 25% for 90m. If minor anomalies, hold and remediate.
- T+150m: Expand to 60% for 120m.
- T+270m: Final expansion to 100% with 2h soak and ramp caps in place.
- Post-24h: Run post-release sample runbook and checklist; collect eval set results and customer-facing telemetry.

HOUR-BY-HOUR CANARY WATCH (quick reference):
- 00:00 — Deploy canary to canary-pool-a (1%): start smoke tests immediately (health checks, token leak, basic latency P50, P95).
- 00:05 — Verify deploy succeeded across three shards; confirm no restart loops.
- 00:15 — Run synthetic traffic (short prompts) and compare response lengths and token counts against baseline.
- 00:30 — Observe latency heatmap; sample logs for 5 most frequent endpoints.
- 00:45 — Check memory and GPU util; ensure no KV eviction spikes.
- 01:00 — Canary decision: green / hold / rollback. Decision owner: release captain (Aisha).

PREFLIGHT CHECKLIST (must be green before T+0):
- [ ] SHA published and pinned in deployment manifest (sha512).
- [ ] Security scan: vulnerabilities <= acceptable threshold.
- [ ] Capacity reserve verified for dedicated pools and burst policy documented.
- [ ] Backfill traffic tests run on staging (traffic replay).
- [ ] Telemetry hooks enabled: token-level counters, model-routing funnel, per-route latency.
- [ ] Canary rollback playbook reviewed and accessible.
- [ ] Pager channels, escalation policy, and on-call rotation confirmed.
- [ ] Ops runbook hyperlinks included in release ticket.

OBSERVABILITY & TELEMETRY (what to watch):
Key signals to monitor during canary and ramp:
- Latency P50 / P95 / P99 by route and region (compare to baseline).
- Error rate (5xx, model-call errors), and user-facing retry surface.
- Token throughput and per-request token variability (batching tweak could increase/decrease tokens per call).
- GPU memory pressure and KV cache miss rate.
- Fallback occurrences: counts of requests routed to fallback variants.
- Cost counters: tokens-per-second and GPU time estimate.
- Quality regression smoke: run 100 curated prompts and diff outputs (automated).

ALERTS & ESCALATION TRIGGERS (suggested thresholds):
- Immediate rollback: sustained 5xx > 0.5% for 15m and >3x baseline.
- Hold and investigate: P95 latency increase >40% for 10m.
- Operator notification: KV eviction rate spike >2x baseline or GPU mem >90% for 5m.
- Quality alarm: >8% of curated eval prompts show tokenization or hallucination variance beyond threshold.

ROLLBACK MATRIX (rapid decision guide):
- Fast rollback (minutes): new binary causes immediate 5xx spike, or API contract break.
- Controlled rollback (30–90m): performance regressions in canary not reproducible in staging — roll back canary, investigate, patch, and replay.
- Gradual unwind: minor cost increase with no user impact — consider throttled rollback or parameter revert.

COMMUNICATION PLAN (internal + external):
- Internal slack channel: #release-garden (pinned runbook). On-call SREs and PM are required.
- Status updates cadence: 00m, +60m, +150m, expansion events and final green. Short bullets only.
- Customer-facing: If any user-visible errors occur, coordinate with CS and PM to prepare status page blurb; default is to notify only after confirming impact.

POST-RELEASE CHECKS & NOTES TEMPLATE (Collect and attach to ticket):
- Summary (one-line): what shipped, why, binary sha.
- Rollout timeline snapshot with decision points.
- Key metrics: P50/P95 latencies, 5xx rate, token throughput, cost delta.
- Quality evaluation: pass/fail on curated prompts + diffs.
- Followups and action items with owners and due dates.
- Suggested retention: store curated eval results and telemetry for 30 days.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (quick bullets):
- Will the KV TTL change interact poorly with long-running chat sessions? (SRE to simulate).
- Prefork warming: could multiply resident set size for small instances (infra to validate).
- Dedicated pool bump: ensure billing/usage tags are correct so cost shows up in billing pipeline.

ACTION ITEMS (owners + target):
- Aisha: finalize runbook and confirm canary SREs (T-48h).
- Liam: publish binary and verify security scan result (T-24h).
- Marisol: telemetry dashboards and synthetic eval harness (T-24h).
- Evelyn: prepare customer-facing status template and CS contact list (T-12h).
- Tomás: preflight staging replay and smoke-run results (T-24h).

QUICK RATIONALE (why this cadence):
- Small initial canary reduces blast radius for serving-runtime changes that affect batching and caches. The multi-step ramp gives us checkpoints to validate cost and quality before full expansion.

MINOR NOTES (notes-to-self style):
- Keep sample eval set immutable for this release so diffs are meaningful.
- If fallback counts spike but latency is stable, inspect routing policy logs — might indicate capacity-triggered flow rather than quality issue.
- Remember to annotate release ticket with relevant dedicated-capacity commit id (billing trace).

ATTACHMENTS / REFERENCES:
- GH PR: redwood/release-engineering#1423 (deploy manifest + small runtime patch)
- JIRA REL-1620 (release request and risk assessment)
- Confluence page: Release-Garden-2026-12 (design notes and eval set).

If anything is unclear or you want to add a specific check, leave a comment on the PR or ping me in slack @aisha.
